events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
The trip was a RydeTAXI metered journey (charged $45.52, distance $31.37 over 22.25 km) with a single off-route segment: 6.56 km driven between 17:38 and 17:49 where the optimal route covers 1.64 km, adding 4.92 km and reaching up to 1911 m off the optimal route [F3][F6]. One unexempted segment would normally trigger RD-2, with the refund computed as extra_km × (distance_fare ÷ distance_km), i.e. 4.92 km × ($31.37 ÷ 22.25 km = $1.4099/km) = $6.94 [F3][F4][F6][RD-2].

But the driver's reason for the deviation — an accident on the Seletar Expressway with lanes blocked — is corroborated by a traffic incident record: an Accident reported at 17:16 on Seletar Expressway (towards TPE) after Woodlands Avenue 12 Exit, located 0 m from the optimal route, i.e. within the 300 m matching radius and on the stretch actually replaced, and reported 22 minutes before the segment began and still live during the trip window [F3][F10][F13][RD-4(a)]. The speed-band record for the same expressway (band 5, 40–49 km/h, 17:17–18:06) does not itself exempt the segment, but it is consistent with congestion on the route and confirms the incident record is not stale [F11][RD-4(b)].

Because RD-4(a) already exempts the segment, no RD-3 or RD-5 consent analysis is required, and the consent scope the trace marks as unnecessary is not needed here [F3][RD-5]. The exempted segment therefore produces no refundable extra km, the metered fare of $45.52 stands, and there is no prior upheld route dispute in the last 90 days (driver: 2 upheld, route: 0), so no account referral arises [F6][F16][RD-6].

The rider's chat is limited to a pickup coordination message and shows no agreement to any route change, which is consistent with the rider never consenting to a change; however, since the deviation is excused by a documented road incident, that absence of consent does not create liability [F7][F9][F10][RD-4(a)].

SAFETY SCREEN: I read every chat message (F7, F8), the driver's statement (F10) and the complaint. Nothing in them constitutes a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; the exchange is ordinary pickup coordination and the statement is a route explanation [F7][F8][F10][SAFE-1].

EVIDENCE: the record settles every element the ruling rests on — the measured off-route segment [F3], the metered fare breakdown [F4][F6], and the time-stamped traffic incident on the replaced stretch [F13] — so the evidence is sufficient.
